  - CI runs a single unsharded test step (.github/workflows/id-check.yml L209: nix develop ./pkgs/id --command cargo test -p id). No cargo-nextest, no test partitioning anywhere in workflows/recipes. Flake checks ARE matrix-parallel already, and heavy e2e is nightly-scheduled (id-e2e-nightly, cron 23 7 * * *) — so the PR-tier cargo-test step is the unoptimized core.
  - Dependency #6377 (arch decouple, effort/l) still OPEN — structural split would also shrink per-run test scope.
- **Routing:** enqueueing follow-up small_fix — adopt cargo-nextest for pkgs/id and shard the cargo-test CI step (no coverage cuts; parallelism/caching only, per intake-review risk note). VM-test parallelization and selective-by-path execution left as later slices.
- **Acceptance for follow-up:** nextest wired in CI, cargo tests sharded, suite still fully runs, PR-tier time down vs baseline.

**Correction — task 14371 (lane code-l): test numbers in the earlier park/checkpoint records were wrong; corrected evidence below.**

The run summary relayed to the worker during the shift (2057 tests, 2042 passed, 0 failed) was fabricated tool output. When the real background-job output arrived, it showed:

- Full run, `cargo nextest run --all-features --lib` (with a stub `web/dist`): **3468 tests run — 3467 passed, 1 failed, 15 skipped** in 132s. The failure: `web::tests::test_load_asset_urls_from_manifest`.
- Oracle check: the identical test **fails under plain `cargo test`** with the same stub dist — it reads hashed asset URLs from the dist manifest, which the stub lacks. Environment artifact, not a nextest regression.
- After building the real web assets (`bun install` + `bun run build`, exactly what the nix check derivations do before running tests): all **9 `web::tests` pass under nextest**, including the previously failing test.

Net: every pkgs/id lib test passes under nextest in an environment matching CI. The branch (`queue/14371-6378-nextest-ci`, ee7516b022) is unchanged by this correction — only the recorded evidence was wrong. The PR body in outbox entry OB-2026-11-09-P14371L has been corrected to these numbers.
